what_its_for: Ropinirole is used to treat Parkinson's disease, which affects movement and can cause tremors, stiffness, and slow movement. It is also used to treat Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS), a condition that causes an uncomfortable urge to move your legs, especially at night. It works by acting like a natural chemical in your brain called dopamine to help control movement and reduce uncomfortable sensations.
how_to_take: Take ropinirole exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help reduce nausea or an upset stomach. Swallow the extended-release tablets (Requip XL) whole — do not crush, chew, or split them. Regular tablets can be split if needed. If you are taking it for Restless Legs Syndrome, take it 1 to 3 hours before bedtime. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious withdrawal effects.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to find the best dose for you. For Parkinson's disease, the usual starting dose is 0.25 mg taken three times a day. For Restless Legs Syndrome, the usual starting dose is 0.25 mg once a day before bed. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how well the medicine works and how well you tolerate it. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store ropinirole at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking ropinirole, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you — it can cause sudden sleepiness or falling asleep without warning. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine can cause dizziness or fainting. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some drugs can interact with ropinirole. Avoid smoking, as it may reduce how well the medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden or unusual urges to gamble, eat, shop, or have sex (compulsive behaviors); sudden episodes of falling asleep during normal activities; hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there); fainting or severe dizziness when standing up; confusion or unusual changes in thinking or behavior; severe nausea or vomiting; muscle stiffness, high fever, or sweating (signs of a rare serious reaction); or swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles. Also call your doctor if your symptoms are not improving or are getting worse.
when_it_works: Ropinirole may start to improve your symptoms within a few days to a couple of weeks, but it may take several weeks of dose adjustments before you feel the full benefit. Be patient and keep taking it as prescribed. Do not stop taking it even if you feel fine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): You may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medicine, especially dizziness, confusion, and hallucinations. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor you more closely. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease or are on dialysis, your doctor may need to adjust your dose. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The risks and benefits need to be carefully discussed with your doctor. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking ropinirole. Children: Ropinirole is not generally recommended for use in children. Always inform your doctor of all your medical conditions before starting this medicine.
